category: Singapore Civil Procedure
title: CLASS ACTIONS UNDER RULES OF COURT 2021
text: Recent amendments to the Supreme Court of Judicature Act and Rules of Court 2021 introduced a structured Class Action Framework. Advise whether [DISPUTE INVOLVING MULTIPLE AFFECTED PERSONS] qualifies for class action treatment. Analyze: (1) whether the case is a "class action" within the statutory definition (common issues of law or fact, class has 50+ members or criteria satisfied); (2) the "test" for certification (commonality, typicality, adequacy of representation, superiority for class action resolution); (3) procedure for obtaining class certification order from court; (4) role of the class representative and class counsel; (5) notification and claims procedures; (6) settlement and approval processes; (7) funding mechanisms including litigation funding. Draft a motion for class certification, including proposed class definition and statement of proposed issues.
context: The Class Action Framework modernizes Singapore's approach to aggregated claims and is modeled partly on comparable regimes in other jurisdictions. Certification is a jurisdictional prerequisite and the court must be satisfied that class action is superior to other methods of resolving the dispute. The framework balances access to justice with court efficiency and protection of absentee class members.
follow_up:
Discuss: (1) likely defendant opposition to certification and key contested issues; (2) funding arrangements with litigation funders; (3) claims administration and notification strategies; (4) potential for settlement and the approval process; (5) appeals of certification decisions.

category: Singapore Civil Procedure
title: CONCURRENT WRITS AND RE-SERVICE
text: [CLIENT'S] Originating Claim against [DEFENDANT] was issued on [DATE], with service validity expiring on [DATE]. Service has not yet been effected due to [REASON - e.g., defendant's difficulty locating, overseas relocation]. Advise on the option to issue a concurrent writ (O6 r4 ROC 2021) and whether this is preferable to seeking an extension of service validity or a fresh Originating Claim. Explain: the procedural requirements for issuing a concurrent writ; how it operates alongside the original writ; cost implications; practical considerations for service. Draft the prayer for issue of a concurrent writ, or advise on the application for extension of service validity under O6 r7 ROC 2021. context: Concurrent writs are useful when original service validity has expired and re-service is required. They must be issued before expiry of original writ validity and must have a corresponding prayer in the Originating Claim. Extensions of service validity are also available but concurrent writs provide a fresher document and separate service validity period.
follow_up:
Discuss: (1) whether defendant may have moved or become harder to locate; (2) costs of re-service attempts; (3) alternative dispute resolution as a parallel track; (4) whether freezing or security measures should be considered.

category: Singapore Civil Procedure
title: GENERAL DISCOVERY AND DISCOVERY DISPUTES
text: Standard disclosure under O26 r1-3 ROC 2021 is due on [DATE]. [CLIENT] is preparing its List of Documents. Advise on: (1) scope of documents to be disclosed (documents "in the possession, custody or power" of [CLIENT], including deleted/destroyed documents with explanation); (2) documents privileged from disclosure (legal advice privilege, litigation privilege, without prejudice communications); (3) documents that should not be disclosed due to confidentiality or public interest immunity; (4) procedure for preparing schedules (Standard Form 11, identifying document, date, author, recipient, brief description); (5) affidavit verifying the list; (6) procedure for inspection of disclosed documents; (7) if [OPPOSING PARTY] has made a discovery request or allegations of non-disclosure, how to respond. Address any dispute regarding scope of disclosure and whether a discovery protocol or tiered/staged disclosure should be implemented. Draft the List of Documents with appropriate assertions of privilege or immunity where necessary.
context: General discovery is mandatory in most civil proceedings and serves to promote fair resolution and prevent trial by surprise. The scope can be modified by agreement between parties. Document production can be a significant cost driver, particularly in digital-heavy disputes. Proper classification of documents (disclosed, privileged, confidential) is essential to avoid waiver of privilege or unintended exposure.
follow_up:

category: Singapore Civil Procedure
title: INTERPLEADER PROCEEDINGS
text: [CLIENT NAME], a [STAKEHOLDER - e.g., insurance company, bailee, agent] holds [ASSET/FUNDS] of value SGD [AMOUNT] to which [CLAIMANT 1] and [CLAIMANT 2] claim entitlement on the basis of [CONFLICTING CLAIMS DESCRIPTION]. [CLIENT] does not itself claim an interest in the asset but wishes to deposit it with the court and be released from liability. Advise on: (1) interpleader proceedings under O17 ROC 2021; (2) prerequisites (no genuine dispute between client and claimants, genuine doubt as to who is entitled, mutual exclusivity of claims); (3) whether the claim should be commenced by Originating Claim or Originating Application; (4) procedure for deposit of the asset; (5) implications if [CLIENT] has a competing claim or genuine doubt of its own. Draft an Originating Claim or Application on an interpleader basis, clearly pleading the conflict and [CLIENT'S] neutrality.
context: Interpleader allows a disinterested stakeholder to seek judicial determination of conflicting claims without becoming involved in the substantive dispute. It requires absence of genuine dispute between the stakeholder and claimants and mutual exclusivity of claims. If the stakeholder has a competing claim, interpleader is unavailable and a multi-party action is required instead.
follow_up:
Address: (1) whether claimants will agree to the interpleader or may resist; (2) security for costs implications; (3) funding and payment of the disputed sum into court; (4) directions needed for trial of the competing claims; (5) recovery of [CLIENT'S] costs from the fund.

category: Singapore Civil Procedure
title: JURISDICTION ANALYSIS: STATE COURTS VS HIGH COURT VS SICC
text: A claim involving [FACTUAL SCENARIO] with an estimated value of [AMOUNT SGD] is contemplated. Analyze the appropriate forum: (1) State Courts (District Court or Magistrates' Court); (2) High Court; or (3) Singapore International Commercial Court (SICC). For each forum, address: jurisdiction and monetary thresholds under the State Courts Act (Cap. 396) and Supreme Court of Judicature Act (Cap. 322); subject matter jurisdiction for equity, defamation, or other specialized disputes; jurisdiction to award damages; procedural differences and rules of court applicable. Consider whether the dispute has international elements and whether SICC would be appropriate under O110 ROC 2021 (international commercial disputes). Provide a recommendation with supporting rationale. Note any tactical implications of forum choice.
context: Forum selection significantly impacts procedure, available remedies, appellate routes, and costs. SICC is increasingly used for international transactions; State Courts are cost-effective for lower-value claims but have jurisdictional caps. High Court is the primary forum for higher-value disputes and specialist matters.
follow_up:
After analysis, discuss: (1) whether any objections to jurisdiction are likely and the strength of such objections; (2) cost-benefit of higher court forum; (3) appeal routes and implications; (4) whether settlement strategy should differ by forum.

category: Singapore Civil Procedure
title: MAREVA INJUNCTION / FREEZING ORDER APPLICATION
text: [CLIENT] has evidence that [DEFENDANT] is likely to dissipate, conceal, or remove assets from [JURISDICTION/COUNTRY] with intent to defeat any judgment that [CLIENT] may obtain in [CASE REFERENCE] or related proceedings. [CLIENT] seeks a Mareva injunction (freezing order) under O29 r3 ROC 2021 to restrain [DEFENDANT] from dealing with assets up to the value of SGD [AMOUNT]. The applicant must establish: (1) a strong prima facie case on the merits; (2) that there is a real risk of dissipation; (3) that the balance of convenience favors granting the order; (4) that there is no alternative remedy; (5) that the court's discretion should be exercised (including public interest considerations). Affidavit evidence addressing each element, including details of the defendant's conduct, asset holdings, and flight risk. The order should be proportionate and include exceptions (living expenses, legal fees, ordinary business expenses). Draft the application and supporting affidavit, addressing the test comprehensively.
context: Mareva injunctions are powerful interim remedies preventing asset dissipation pending trial. They require careful application as they are interlocutory and may affect the defendant's livelihood if too broad. The standard is demanding: "strong" prima facie case and "real risk" of dissipation (not merely possibility). Orders are often granted on a without-notice basis initially to preserve their effect, followed by inter partes hearing.
follow_up:
Discuss: (1) whether to apply without notice (ex parte) initially or on notice; (2) undertaking in damages required from the applicant; (3) scope of the order and exceptions (family living expenses, business operations); (4) disclosure obligations and updating affidavits; (5) variation or discharge applications if circumstances change; (6) ancillary orders (disclosure of assets, bank account information); (7) implications of breach of the order.

category: Singapore Civil Procedure
title: ORIGINATING APPLICATION ANALYSIS
text: Advise whether [DISPUTE DESCRIPTION] should proceed by Originating Application (Form 7) rather than Originating Claim (Form 8) under Rules of Court 2021. category: Singapore Civil Procedure
title: STRIKING OUT PROCEEDINGS
text: [OPPOSING PARTY'S] pleading (being [Originating Claim/Defence/Counterclaim/Reply]) contains [DEFECT DESCRIPTION]. [CLIENT] seeks to strike out the pleading or parts thereof under O18 r8 ROC 2021 on the grounds that: (1) it discloses no reasonable cause of action/defence; (2) it is frivolous or vexatious; (3) it constitutes an abuse of process; and/or (4) [OTHER GROUND - e.g., procedural defect]. The pleading fails to [SPECIFIC FAILURE - e.g., "particularize the alleged breach with dates and amounts," "establish causation between the act complained of and the loss claimed"]. Draft an application to strike out with detailed affidavit evidence addressing each ground, identifying the specific paragraphs or passages that are objectionable, and explaining why each is unmaintainable. Include proposed alternative relief (striking out with leave to amend) if appropriate.
context: Striking out is a drastic remedy available only when the defect is patent and self-evident from the pleading itself, without requiring investigation of facts. It is not available merely because the pleading is weak on the merits or inadequately supported by evidence (which is addressed through summary judgment or at trial). Courts approach striking out applications cautiously to avoid denying parties their right to litigate.
follow_up:
Address: (1) whether the defect can be cured by amendment and, if so, whether to offer leave to amend; (2) procedures and timelines for any amendment; (3) costs recovery if striking out is successful; (4) any threshold objections to jurisdiction or service that should be dealt with first; (5) whether striking out should be pursued or whether summary judgment is a more efficient remedy.

title: SUMMARY JUDGMENT APPLICATION
text: [CLIENT - CLAIMANT/DEFENDANT] seeks summary judgment on [CLAIM/DEFENCE] in proceedings [CASE REFERENCE]. The [OPPOSING PARTY] has filed [DEFENCE/COUNTERCLAIM] alleging [DEFENCE SUMMARY]. [CLIENT] contends that there is no triable issue of fact and [OPPOSING PARTY] has no real prospect of success because [SUBSTANTIVE ARGUMENT - 1-2 sentences]. Apply the test under O14 ROC 2021 (if State Courts) or O13 ROC 2021 (if High Court), addressing: (1) whether [OPPOSING PARTY] has a real prospect of success (not just an arguable case); (2) whether there is a triable issue of fact; (3) whether there are compelling reasons for a trial despite meeting the test; (4) the strength and credibility of affidavit evidence. Prepare a supporting affidavit with exhibits (documents, correspondence, expert opinion if available) and draft the prayer for summary judgment. Address anticipated defences and why they do not raise a triable issue.
context: Summary judgment (called "summons for directions" in some contexts) is a critical interlocutory remedy allowing parties to obtain judgment without trial when the opposing party has no real prospect of success. The threshold is high: the opposing party must have more than a fanciful case but need not be strong on the merits. Court considers whether a trial would truly add value.
follow_up:
Discuss: (1) likely grounds of opposition and counter-arguments; (2) whether partial summary judgment (on some issues) is achievable; (3) whether conditional judgment (summary judgment on liability with quantum to trial) should be sought; (4) costs implications and recovery of costs; (5) timing of application and impact on case progression.
